day_shape: 66 items: third consecutive night of CENTCOM strikes on Iran and reinstated Hormuz blockade, UK moves to designate the IRGC under state threats law, tanker attacks in Omani waters, Houthi strike reported on Abha airport, no IAEA output.

threads.label: US-Iran strikes and Hormuz blockade
threads.summary: CENTCOM announced a third consecutive night of strikes on Iran beginning 4:45pm ET and said sea drones hit Bandar Abbas Naval Base in a combat first. Trump notified Congress the US had resumed military action, reinstated a naval blockade, and said the US would 'probably take over' the Strait of Hormuz.

threads.label: Tanker attacks and Gulf response
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported two UAE-flagged tankers and one British tanker were struck in Omani waters of the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil up more than 3%. The UAE was reported to be planning a port on the opposite side of Hormuz to bypass Iranian closure, with a Bahraini analyst saying Gulf patience was being tested.

threads.label: UK designates IRGC under state threats law
threads.summary: The UK government announced the IRGC, the Islamic Movement of Companions of the Right, and a third body would be designated under the National Security Act, making support a criminal offence subject to parliamentary approval this week. Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper and the Home Office laid draft regulations and sanctioned the IMCR over attacks on Jewish locations.

threads.label: Yemen: Houthi strikes and UNSC meeting
threads.summary: Local Saudi media reported Houthi missiles targeting Abha International Airport, and Saudi Arabia was reported to have begun striking near Sanaa International Airport. The UN Security Council held an emergency meeting on unauthorised Iranian flights into Sana'a and Hudaydah, with UK Chargé d'Affaires Kate Foster condemning the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

threads.label: Gaza: aid warehouse assault and recovery funding
threads.summary: The IDF and UN reports said Hamas operatives forcibly entered a WFP warehouse in Jabalia on 11 July and assaulted two drivers, prompting a UN condemnation of 'de facto authorities'. The UK announced £10 million for Palestinian-led early recovery, and the EU unveiled a $1 billion Gaza recovery initiative for water, sanitation and debris clearance.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and Sinwar documents
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Hamas naval-force cell commander Osama Naim Hamdi Shamlakh in a Gaza City strike and weapons smuggler Mustafa Owaisi in the south. Newly released documents reported by Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post said Yahya Sinwar assessed before 7 October that Israel might respond with a nuclear strike on Gaza.

threads.label: Ahmadinejad-Mossad recruitment report
threads.summary: Haaretz reported, citing more than 30 sources, that Mossad recruited former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and planned to install him after an operation against the Islamic Republic. The Jerusalem Post reported Ahmadinejad was under house arrest by IRGC intelligence, while his office denied the account.

A separate strike in northern Gaza killed three armed Hamas gunmen who the military says were advancing attacks on troops. "The terrorists posed an imminent threat to the troops and were eliminated in precise aerial strikes," the IDF adds.
